about: Twelve fictional alerts based on public alert types: six escalate and six close. The scenarios and labels are for this classroom experiment, not real organizational logs.
extra_fields: event_type, asset, account, change_id, and time_utc are simulated log fields used by the read-only context tool. expected and note are withheld from the graph.
hard_cases: M05: incident with none of the eleven tested keywords
M07: approved lab exercise containing ransomware
M06: mailbox incident missed by every configuration

alerts.alert: EDR detected ransomware rewriting finance documents on FIN-LT-04 while the employee was using the laptop.
alerts.note: Files are being changed on a production laptop during normal use; this needs an immediate analyst review.

alerts.alert: A critical RCE alert on WEB-01 was followed by an unexpected process launched by the public web service.
alerts.note: The unexpected child process adds evidence that the exposed service may have been exploited.

alerts.alert: Cloud audit logs show an admin role granted to a regular user without an approved change, and the user denies requesting it.
alerts.note: An unapproved increase in access needs investigation, especially when the user denies the action.

alerts.alert: Repeated MFA prompts ended with a sign-in from an unfamiliar device, and the employee says they did not approve it.
alerts.note: Repeated prompts plus an unfamiliar successful session suggest account misuse.

alerts.alert: Successful VPN session for a departed employee; no current owner approved the activity.
alerts.note: This account belongs to someone who left the organization. A successful session needs review even though no tested keyword appears.

alerts.alert: A mailbox rule now sends copies of payroll messages to an unfamiliar personal inbox; the owner denies creating it.
alerts.note: The rule could expose payroll information. None of the tested keywords appears, and the current context tool does not check forwarding destinations.

alerts.alert: Ransomware test detection on LAB-WS-01 matched an authorized exercise; no production files were touched.
alerts.note: The lab target, simulation event, and time match approved record CHG-1042. This is the routine alert that contains a keyword.

alerts.alert: Administrator installed a signed update on APP-02 during the approved maintenance window.
alerts.note: The target, patch event, and time match approved record CHG-1043; this is expected maintenance.

alerts.alert: One failed sign-in on a managed laptop was followed by a successful sign-in from the same device, and the employee confirmed a typing mistake.
alerts.note: The single failure is explained by the user and followed by normal activity; there are no other suspicious signals in this example.

alerts.alert: The employee completed a password reset through the normal self-service page and confirmed the request with the help desk.
alerts.note: The user confirmed a routine reset through the approved process.

alerts.alert: A scheduled backup finished with one skipped temporary folder, which the system owner confirmed was excluded from the backup plan.
alerts.note: The warning matches an intended exclusion and does not describe a security incident.

alerts.alert: MFA device registration matched the verified ticket for an employee replacement phone, and the employee confirmed the setup.
alerts.note: The phone replacement was verified. The limited lookup tool only supports the lab exercise and patch approvals, so it cannot use this help-desk evidence.
